chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the man divorces his wife while he is healthy (not in the deathbed illness), and there is no retraction (revocation of divorce) for him regarding her, she does not inherit him and he does not inherit her.
And he (peace be upon him) said: He inherits and is inherited as long as she does not see the blood of the third menstruation, if there is a retraction for him regarding her.

key_terms.صَحِيح: Healthy (referring to the husband's state, not in deathbed illness)

ai.seo_question: Does a divorced wife inherit from her husband during the waiting period if he dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the inheritance rights of a wife during the 'Iddah' period, distinguishing between revocable (Raj'i) and irrevocable (Ba'in) divorces. It establishes that if the divorce is revocable, the wife inherits from her husband until the third menstrual cycle is completed, provided no blood is seen, reflecting the principle that the marital bond remains partially intact. This ruling is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the distribution of estate during the waiting period following a revocable divorce.
